source_snapshot.test_name_items: All HDD NVMe LED Check - Raid fail
source_snapshot.procedure:
【Before Test】
    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
    Check if NVMe RAID fail LED function works normally

1. Insert NVMe SSD into BP slot and create RAID 1
2. Unplug one NVMe SSD from RAID group
3. Check RAID fail LED

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.
source_snapshot.criteria: 1. Check system spec define LED function

deepseek_columns.ai_commands: Undocumented raw IPMI bytes plus `lsblk` inventory.
deepseek_columns.ai_logs_output: Management result, device list and physical Fail LED observation.

historical_reviews.deepseek: PARTIAL; does not build RAID 1, remove a member or establish failure and provides unvalidated raw BMC bytes.
historical_reviews.gpt_v2: REQUIRES PACKAGE / USER CONFIRMATION / CHANGED; adds disposable media, destructive approval, healthy baseline, physical fault, degraded telemetry and separate recovery.

original_test_intent: For the project-defined NVMe HDD population, create an isolated RAID 1, physically remove an approved member and verify the correct specification-defined RAID-fail indicator together with degraded-array evidence.
original_method: Build RAID 1 only on disposable serial-allowlisted drives, confirm healthy synchronization and bay mapping, have an operator unplug the exact member, then correlate physical Fail LED media with controller/OS/BMC degraded events; recovery is a separate approval.
manual_activity: The required failure is a physical member unplug and the accepted output is a visible Fail LED. Both are human core actions even though RAID creation and degraded monitoring can be automated.
required_inputs: Controller RAID 1 parameters and disposable SSD serials with no protected data
Exact member/bay removal map and supported hot-remove procedure
Fail LED state/timing and expected controller degraded event
safety_requirements: Never create the array on boot, mounted, in-use, protected, data-bearing or unknown drives.
Verify a healthy synchronized RAID 1 and exact member/bay identity before removal.
Only a qualified operator performs the documented unplug.
Do not use raw IPMI bytes to fabricate the failure indicator or touch unrelated management state.
No automatic reinsert, rebuild, delete, initialize or retry; preserve the degraded state/evidence.
agent_execution_scope: Validate the population, destructive plan and pre-state, then create RAID 1 only if explicitly authorized.
Prove healthy baseline and display exact member mapping before the operator acts.
Capture degraded controller/OS/BMC events and correlate physical evidence for each tested configuration.
Report per-configuration Tool Results without claiming unplug/LED or verdict.
engineer_actions: Approve disposable targets, array creation, exact physical removal and recovery.
Unplug the approved member and visually record the Fail LED.
Authorize post-test recovery and issue PASS/FAIL.

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: Non-equivalent: raw IPMI and `lsblk` do not create RAID 1 or member failure, do not prove the physical Fail LED, and have no validated target mapping.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Use controller-native build/read-only degraded-state commands for the approved hardware; retain physical unplug and visual evidence as authoritative.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: All-HDD NVMe scope, RAID 1, one-member unplug, Fail LED check and 15/8-minute fields are preserved.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Use an approved serial/bay/array matrix, synchronized controller event capture and operator video for each required member-removal configuration.
modernized_recommendation.applicable_platform: Exact NVMe RAID controller, backplane and fail-indicator implementation.
modernized_recommendation.supported_version: Record controller/backplane/BMC firmware, OS driver and utility versions.
modernized_recommendation.official_reference: Controller degraded-array and platform Fail LED/hot-remove documentation.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds safe all-population traceability and rejects unverified BMC manipulation.
modernized_recommendation.required_inputs: Population, truth table and recovery plan.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: CLI degradation and visible LED are complementary; neither proves the other.

project_override_considerations: The project may define a representative `all HDD` matrix, but each claimed configuration must be listed and must include real removal plus physical Fail LED evidence.
expected_evidence: Population/mapping, disposable-drive proof, destructive approval and healthy array baseline
RAID 1 build/sync transcript and exact member-to-bay mapping
Operator removal timestamp/video and matching degraded-member events
Post-state/recovery decision, OS/BMC logs, Tool Result and engineer verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Procedure and criterion coherently test a specification-defined failure indicator after RAID 1 member removal. Population details are missing inputs.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The operation is clear and executable once disposable targets, safe physical procedure and recovery are supplied.

comparison_to_prior_reviews.deepseek: Rejects its raw-command/inventory shortcut as missing the actual failure path.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.gpt_v2: Retains its critical storage controls; applies MANUAL ONLY for physical fault and observation.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.v3_1_improvement: Requires explicit all-HDD coverage and separately tracks degradation, physical evidence and verdict.

review_improvement: Prevents management output from being misreported as a destructive physical failure/LED test and makes coverage auditable.
independent_technical_reasoning: The controller can automate array configuration and telemetry, but the specified stimulus and observation are physical. Their centrality fixes the class at MANUAL ONLY.
no_automatic_retry: Do not repeat removal or automatically reinsert/rebuild/delete/recreate after any anomaly. Preserve the first fault and await owner direction.
